findings.text: The old escaping of ESC to  was removed, and only SGR color codes (ESC[...m) are stripped. Any other ESC byte, such as the cursor sequence ESC[2K or ESC[1;31;m, now reaches the XML output raw. ESC is invalid in XML 1.0, so JUnit parsers will reject the report.

raw:
Issues: other escape sequences (non-color) now leave raw ESC in XML, which is invalid XML 1.0. Also `[0-9;]+m` regex: BASH_REMATCH used as a glob pattern in the substitution; `[` in it is a glob bracket, so `\033[31m` is treated as a bracket expression and may not match literally. This could cause an infinite loop.

The pattern `${output//${BASH_REMATCH[0]}/}` is unquoted, so the match `ESC[31m` is read as the glob `ESC` + `[31m]`... The bracket `[31m` has no closing `]`, so bash treats it literally, and it works. With `ESC[0;1m`, the same applies. A closing `]` never appears in the match, so the loop terminates. The remaining issue is the ESC handling.
